messages:
maria: quick q — what's the recommended pattern for mounting API keys into k8s pods vs passing them as env vars? seeing intermittent 401s when our service builds Basic auth header

sam: mounts are fine for rotation (you can update the secret) but file-newlines are the usual headache. env is simpler but harder to rotate without restart

maria: we mount a secret, read with Go os.ReadFile, then build header with base64 of `fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%s\", username, apikey)` — username is empty. some requests 401, others fine

lee: can you paste the code you use to base64? also how the secret is created (kubectl or external vault)?

maria: simple: `auth := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%s\", username, apikey)))` then header `Authorization: Basic ` + auth. secret created via k8s Secret (kubectl create secret generic) from a CI artifact

anita: two obvious suspects: 1) trailing newline in the file, 2) CRLF from windows. note: if username empty you must encode `\":\" + apikey` (so `fmt.Sprintf(\":%s\", apikey)`) — colons inside the apikey itself are valid, they just become part of the password field

maria: ah, we didn't strip newline. how do people reliably strip JUST the newline (not other whitespace) across languages?

sam: CLI helpers: `tr -d '\n'` or use `base64 -w0` when generating. In Go prefer `bytes.TrimSuffix(b, []byte(\"\n\"))` or `bytes.TrimRight(b, \"\n\")` to avoid removing spaces. `strings.TrimSpace` will also drop tabs/spaces which you might not want

lee: Node: `const key = fs.readFileSync('/var/secrets/key', 'utf8').replace(/\n$/, '')` — that only removes a single trailing LF. For CRLF do `.replace(/\r?\n$/, '')`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: secret rotated in staging at 2024-11-05T12:02:00Z — watch for rollouts :rocket:

anita: and watch shell quoting: if the key has `$` or `!` or spaces, export carefully. e.g. `KEY=$(cat /var/secrets/key)` then `curl -u :"$KEY"` or better build header explicitly

maria: about curl — is `curl -u :$KEY` equivalent to `-H 'Authorization: Basic <base64>'`? any edge cases with colons in KEY?

sam: yes, curl treats `:` as empty user and everything after as password. If KEY contains colons that's fine — curl will base64 encode the combined string `:password` including any `:` in the password. The only risk is shell splitting/expansion. Use single quotes or pass via file or `--netrc` if you can

lee: example one-liner to build header safely: `curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $(printf \":%s\" \"$KEY\" | base64 -w0)\" https://api.redwood.ai` — `-w0` avoids newline from base64. On mac `base64` flags differ (`-b 0`), so use `openssl base64 -A` if needed

maria: solid. we'll switch to TrimSuffix in Go and add a unit test with keys that contain `:` and trailing `\n`. also add CI check for windows CRLF import. thanks :pray:
__notes: generated for devex; focuses on k8s secret file mount vs env var and Basic auth header construction. messages are short and Slack-like per agents.md rules
